symbols.type: A pair of probability vectors on \(\mathcal I\)

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: \(V=(V_x:x\in T)\), where \(V_x\) is the well-defined outcome under category \(x\) and is shared across instrument arms.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: \(W=(W_{xz}:x\in U,z\in\{0,1\})\), with no cross-arm equality imposed.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Q_T(p)\) is the set of response laws compatible with \(p\) under the mixed-trust observation map.

symbols.name: relation
symbols.type: A binary relation on \(\mathcal I\times\mathcal I\)

symbols.name: Pi
symbols.def: \(\Pi_T(p)\) is the set of nonnegative matrices on \(\mathfrak R_T\) with row margins \(p^0\) and column margins \(p^1\).

symbols.name: pbar
symbols.type: A pair of probability vectors on \(\mathcal I\)

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: \((\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_8)\) are the eight Balke--Pearl lower pieces in the displayed construction \(\mathfrak F^-_T(p)\).

symbols.name: Cminus
symbols.type: Two affine functionals per trusted nuisance category

symbols.name: Cplus
symbols.type: Two affine functionals per trusted nuisance category

symbols.name: Fminus
symbols.type: A finite set of affine functionals

symbols.name: Fplus
symbols.type: A finite set of affine functionals

symbols.name: qLower
symbols.def: \(q^-_T(p)\) is the law returned by the lower endpoint-attainment construction.

symbols.name: qUpper
symbols.def: \(q^+_T(p)\) is obtained by applying the lower construction to \(\bar p\) and reversing every binary outcome.

symbols.name: cstar
symbols.def: On the specialization \(\mathcal E=\{a,b,c_\star\}\), \(c_\star\) is the unique nuisance category.

symbols.name: rSep
symbols.role: Nuisance-category exposure masses in the separation family

symbols.name: sSep
symbols.role: Target-category allocation shares in the separation family

symbols.name: tauSep
symbols.role: Trusted target-outcome probabilities in the separation family

symbols.name: lambdaSep
symbols.role: Arm-specific untrusted outcome probabilities in the separation family

symbols.name: Asep
symbols.role: Exposure masses for category \(a\) in the separation family

symbols.name: Bsep
symbols.role: Exposure masses for category \(b\) in the separation family

symbols.name: qSep
symbols.def: \(q^{\rm sep}_{r,s,\tau,\lambda}\) is the selected-trust response law in the perturbation-stable strict-regime construction.

symbols.name: pSep
symbols.type: A pair of probability vectors on \(\mathcal I\)
symbols.def: \(p^{\rm sep}\) is the observed table induced by the perturbation-stable family \(q^{\rm sep}_{r,s,\tau,\lambda}\) under the mixed-trust observation map.

symbols.name: pGain
symbols.type: A pair of probability vectors on \(\mathcal I\)
symbols.def: \(p^{\rm gain}\) is the strictly tightening three-category table in the strict-regime construction.

symbols.name: etaGain
symbols.def: \(\eta_{\rm gain}>0\) is an open-neighborhood radius derived in \(\text{thm:strict-regime-separation}\).

symbols.name: cnew
symbols.def: \(c\) is the nuisance category newly declared trusted.

symbols.name: Eref
symbols.def: \(\widetilde{\mathcal E}\) is a refinement of \(\mathcal E\).

symbols.name: Tref
symbols.def: \(\widetilde T\) contains the unique preimages of the trusted categories and no refined child of an untrusted category.

symbols.name: pref
symbols.def: \(\widetilde p\) satisfies \(p^z_{xy}=\sum_{\tilde x:g(\tilde x)=x}\widetilde p^z_{\tilde x y}\).

symbols.name: phat
symbols.type: A pair of empirical probability vectors

symbols.name: alphaConf
symbols.def: \(\alpha_{\rm conf}\) is the desired simultaneous error probability.

symbols.name: Mfaces
symbols.role: Number of simultaneously controlled affine pieces

symbols.name: coef
symbols.def: Each affine face has the representation \(f(p)=b_f+\sum_{z=0}^1\mathbb E_P[a_{fz}(X,Y)\mid Z=z]\).

symbols.name: endpointBox
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{\rm end}=[L_{\rm lo},L_{\rm hi}]\times[U_{\rm lo},U_{\rm hi}]\), where \(L_{\rm lo}=\max_{f\in\mathfrak F^-_T}\{f(\widehat p)-\varepsilon_f\}\), \(L_{\rm hi}=\max_{f\in\mathfrak F^-_T}\{f(\widehat p)+\varepsilon_f\}\), \(U_{\rm lo}=\min_{f\in\mathfrak F^+_T}\{f(\widehat p)-\varepsilon_f\}\), and \(U_{\rm hi}=\min_{f\in\mathfrak F^+_T}\{f(\widehat p)+\varepsilon_f\}\).

symbols.name: wholeSetCI
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{\rm set}=[L_{\rm lo},U_{\rm hi}]\cap[-1,1]\), with \([-1,1]\) returned if an instrument arm is empty.
symbols.role: Outer confidence interval for the whole sharp set

symbols.name: rhoBar
symbols.def: \(\bar\rho\) is the allocation floor in the Gaussian outlook.

symbols.name: PTri
symbols.type: A class of triangular arrays of multinomial laws
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak A_T(\bar\rho)=\{(P_n)_{n\geq1}:P_n\text{ is multinomial with arm probabilities }p_n,\ \rho_n\in[\bar\rho,1-\bar\rho],\ \mathcal Q_T(p_n)\neq\varnothing\text{ for every }n\}\).
symbols.role: Uniformity domain for the Gaussian outlook

symbols.name: regularConstants
symbols.def: \(\varepsilon_{\rm reg}>0\), \(\gamma_{\rm reg}>0\), and \(\sigma^2_{\rm reg}>0\) are respectively a cell floor, an active-face separation, and an active-face variance floor.

symbols.name: regularClass
symbols.type: A compact set of multinomial laws
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K(\varepsilon_{\rm reg},\gamma_{\rm reg},\sigma^2_{\rm reg})\) is any nonempty compact class of \(T\)-compatible laws with \(\rho\in[\bar\rho,1-\bar\rho]\), arm cells at least \(\varepsilon_{\rm reg}\), a unique active affine face at each endpoint separated from every other face by at least \(\gamma_{\rm reg}\), and both active-face variances at least \(\sigma^2_{\rm reg}\).

symbols.name: GaussianBox
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C^G_n=[L^G_{\rm lo},L^G_{\rm hi}]\times[U^G_{\rm lo},U^G_{\rm hi}]\) is the endpoint rectangle returned by the boundary-spliced active-face multiplier handle.

symbols.name: totalWidth
symbols.type: A nonnegative functional on endpoint rectangles
symbols.def: For \(\mathcal C=[l_{\rm lo},l_{\rm hi}]\times[u_{\rm lo},u_{\rm hi}]\), set \(w_{\rm tot}(\mathcal C)=(l_{\rm hi}-l_{\rm lo})+(u_{\rm hi}-u_{\rm lo})\).

symbols.name: GaussianHandle
symbols.def: For fixed finite \((\mathcal E,T)\), \(\alpha_{\rm conf}\), and \(\bar\rho\), start from the shared multiplier empirical process of all affine faces, estimate the max/min directional derivative on a self-normalized near-active face set, and splice in \(\mathcal C_{\rm end}\) whenever a relevant estimated face variance degenerates.
symbols.role: Starting move for sharper tie-robust inference

standard.name: Compatibility of the observed law with a finite IV response model

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P\).

standard.name: Independent and identically distributed multinomial sampling

definitions.name: Mixed-trust observation map
definitions.construction: Draw \(R=(X_0,X_1,V,W)\sim q\) and \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), set \(X=X_Z\), and set \(Y=V_X\) if \(X\in T\) and \(Y=W_{XZ}\) if \(X\in U\).

definitions.name: Compatible response laws
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q_T(p)=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal R_T):\Pr_q(X_z=x,\,V_x=y)=p^z_{xy}\text{ for }x\in T;\ \Pr_q(X_z=x,\,W_{xz}=y)=p^z_{xy}\text{ for }x\in U,\ z,y\in\{0,1\}\}\).

definitions.name: Complete affine evaluation list
definitions.construction: \(\ell_1=-1+\alpha_1+\beta_1\), \(\ell_2=-1+\alpha_1+\beta_0\), \(\ell_3=-1+\alpha_0+\beta_0\), \(\ell_4=-1+\alpha_0+\beta_1\), \(\ell_5=-2+2\alpha_0+\gamma_1+\beta_0+\beta_1\), \(\ell_6=-2+\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\delta_0+2\beta_1\), \(\ell_7=-2+2\alpha_1+\gamma_0+\beta_0+\beta_1\), \(\ell_8=-2+\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\delta_1+2\beta_0\); then \(\mathfrak F^-_T=\{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_8\}\cup\{\kappa-h_{cy}:c\in T\setminus\{a,b\},y\in\{0,1\}\}\) and \(\mathfrak F^+_T\) is its outcome-reversed negative.

definitions.name: Finite endpoint-attainment algorithm
definitions.construction: For the lower endpoint reserve \(r_s=\min\{u,D_T(p)\}\) on edge \((s,s)\) and \(r_t=D_T(p)-r_s\) on edge \((t,t)\); subtract these masses from the corresponding margins, complete the residual transport on \(\mathfrak R_T\) by finite augmenting paths, and on each supported edge set every observed trusted potential outcome to its factual value, every unobserved \(V_a\) to \(1\), every unobserved \(V_b\) to \(0\), all other unobserved trusted values to \(0\), and the observed untrusted \(W\)-slots to their factual values. The upper law applies the same algorithm to \(\bar p\) and reverses all outcome bits.

definitions.name: Selected-trust separation and gain witnesses
definitions.construction: Specialize to \(\mathcal E=\{a,b,c_\star\}\), \(T_0=\{a,b\}\), and \(\rho=1/2\). Choose \(r_0,r_1\in(31/50,17/25)\), \(s_0,s_1,\tau_a,\tau_b\in(2/5,3/5)\), \(\lambda_0\in(3/100,7/100)\), and \(\lambda_1\in(93/100,97/100)\), and put \(A_z=(1-r_z)s_z\) and \(B_z=(1-r_z)(1-s_z)\). Under \(q^{\rm sep}_{r,s,\tau,\lambda}\), let \(X_0\) and \(X_1\) be independent categorical variables with \(\Pr(X_z=a)=A_z\), \(\Pr(X_z=b)=B_z\), and \(\Pr(X_z=c_\star)=r_z\); independently draw \(V_a\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\tau_a)\), \(V_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\tau_b)\), \(W_{c_\star0}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\lambda_0)\), and \(W_{c_\star1}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\lambda_1)\). Its observed table is \(p^{{\rm sep},z}_{a0}=A_z(1-\tau_a)\), \(p^{{\rm sep},z}_{a1}=A_z\tau_a\), \(p^{{\rm sep},z}_{b0}=B_z(1-\tau_b)\), \(p^{{\rm sep},z}_{b1}=B_z\tau_b\), \((p^{{\rm sep},0}_{c_\star0},p^{{\rm sep},0}_{c_\star1})=(r_0(1-\lambda_0),r_0\lambda_0)\), and \((p^{{\rm sep},1}_{c_\star0},p^{{\rm sep},1}_{c_\star1})=(r_1(1-\lambda_1),r_1\lambda_1)\). Define \(p^{\rm gain}\), in cell order \((a,0),(a,1),(b,0),(b,1),(c_\star,0),(c_\star,1)\), by \[p^{{\rm gain},0}=\tfrac1{10}(1,1,1,1,5,1),\qquad p^{{\rm gain},1}=\tfrac1{10}(1,1,1,1,2,4).\]

definitions.name: Wholly untrusted refinement
definitions.construction: A surjection \(g:\widetilde{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal E\) is wholly untrusted when every \(x\in T\) has a unique preimage in \(\widetilde T\), no element of \(g^{-1}(U)\) belongs to \(\widetilde T\), and \(\widetilde p\) pushes forward to \(p\) arm by arm.

definitions.name: Finite-sample whole-set band
definitions.construction: Represent every \(f\in\mathfrak F^-_T\cup\mathfrak F^+_T\) by its armwise coefficient functions, compute \(\varepsilon_f\), form \(\mathcal C_{\rm end}\), and report \(\mathcal C_{\rm set}\); if \(N_0N_1=0\), report the trivial endpoint box and \([-1,1]\).

definitions.name: Boundary-spliced active-face multiplier handle
definitions.construction: For fixed finite \((\mathcal E,T)\), \(\alpha_{\rm conf}\), and \(\bar\rho>0\), use the shared multiplier process for all faces, a self-normalized estimated near-active set for the max/min directional derivative, and the Hoeffding endpoint rectangle as the splice on variance-degenerate faces, returning \(\mathcal C^G_n\).

statements.statement: Every \(q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\) induces a coupling \(\pi\in\Pi_T(p)\) of the two factual responses. Conversely, every \(\pi\in\Pi_T(p)\) lifts by finite edgewise completion to a law \(q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\). Under this lift, the smallest attainable contribution of edge \((i,j)\) to \(\theta_{ab}\) is \(d^-(i,j)\), and therefore \(\inf_{q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)}\theta_{ab}(q)=\kappa-\sup_{\pi\in\Pi_T(p)}(\pi_{ss}+\pi_{tt})\).
statements.justification: This is the structural reduction that turns the response-type projection into a two-diagonal transport problem.
statements.gap: Song et al. couple each factual arm to a full vector of potential outcomes under global exclusion; they do not provide this direct two-arm partial-matching reduction under selected trust.
statements.consumer: It supplies the proof engine for closed-form bounds and constructive response laws without enumerating \(|\mathcal E|^2 2^{|T|+2|U|}\) saturated types.

statements.statement: The polytope \(\Pi_T(p)\) is nonempty if and only if \(p\) is armwise normalized and \(p^0_{xy}+p^1_{x,1-y}\leq1\) for every \(x\in T\) and \(y\in\{0,1\}\). After reserving nonnegative masses \(r_s\) and \(r_t\) on \((s,s)\) and \((t,t)\), the residual coupling exists if and only if \(r_s\leq u\), \(r_t\leq v\), and \(r_s+r_t\leq h_{cy}\) for every trusted nuisance cell; these conditions include all boundary strata.
statements.justification: The singleton Hall cuts of a complete bipartite graph minus a partial matching yield exactly the individual and total residual caps.
statements.gap: Full-exclusion observed compatibility is known, but the residual-cap statement after reserving target diagonals is the unverified completion step specific to the proposed projection.
statements.consumer: A finite augmenting-path construction from these conditions certifies every endpoint law, including zero cells and saturated inequalities.

statements.statement: For every compatible \(p\), the identified set \(\{\theta_{ab}(q):q\in\mathcal Q_T(p)\}\) is exactly \([L_T(p),U_T(p)]\), where \(L_T(p)=\kappa-D_T(p)=\max_{f\in\mathfrak F^-_T}f(p)\) and \(U_T(p)=-L_T(\bar p)=\min_{f\in\mathfrak F^+_T}f(p)\). Each endpoint list contains the eight Balke--Pearl affine pieces and exactly two additional evaluation pieces \(C^-_{c,0},C^-_{c,1}\), or \(C^+_{c,0},C^+_{c,1}\), for every \(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\}\); no affine inequality involving several nuisance categories lowers or raises an endpoint beyond this envelope. The finite laws \(q^-_T(p)\) and \(q^+_T(p)\) attain the two endpoints, and their mixtures attain every interior value. As a one-line corollary, if \(T'=T\cup\{c\}\) is compatible, then \(L_{T'}(p)=\max\{L_T(p),C^-_{c,0}(p),C^-_{c,1}(p)\}\) and \(U_{T'}(p)=\min\{U_T(p),C^+_{c,0}(p),C^+_{c,1}(p)\}\), with strict width reduction exactly when \(\max_yC^-_{c,y}(p)>L_T(p)\) or \(\min_yC^+_{c,y}(p)<U_T(p)\).
statements.justification: This theorem resolves the arbitrary-cardinality mixed-validity projection and isolates the linear-size closed form.
statements.gap: Gabriel et al. stop at small treatment supports, while Song et al. require exclusion at every category and leave the pairwise effect as a general optimization.
statements.consumer: The theorem lets LEAP investigators decide whether separately defensible intermediate adherence interventions can change the low-versus-high interval without rerunning symbolic polyhedral elimination.

statements.statement: If \(T=\{a,b\}\), then \(D_T(p)=u+v\) and \([L_T(p),U_T(p)]\) is exactly the Balke--Pearl binary-exposure envelope evaluated on the two target cells while all remaining exposure mass is unrestricted. If \(|\mathcal E|=3\) and \(T=\mathcal E\), the two nuisance-category pieces reproduce the published Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander ternary formulas. If \(T=\mathcal E\) for arbitrary finite \(\mathcal E\), the interval is the pairwise ATE projection of the fully valid categorical-IV model characterized by Song et al.
statements.justification: The reductions enforce comparator fidelity and the required binary and ternary sanity checks.
statements.gap: The reductions are known separately, but their simultaneous appearance as boundaries of one selected-trust formula must be verified algebraically.
statements.consumer: Existing binary and ternary software can use these equalities as regression tests for the arbitrary-support evaluator.

statements.statement: In the three-category specialization \(\mathcal E=\{a,b,c_\star\}\), selected trust and full exclusion are separated by a perturbation-stable generic obstruction, and trusting \(c_\star\) yields a strict bound gain on a separate nondegenerate open region. For every parameter choice in \(q^{\rm sep}_{r,s,\tau,\lambda}\), the displayed construction belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{T_0}(p^{\rm sep})\), every observed cell exceeds \(93/5000\), and, for \(x\in\{a,b\}\), every compatibility sum obeys \(p^{{\rm sep},0}_{xy}+p^{{\rm sep},1}_{x,1-y}<57/125\). Full exclusion is impossible because its necessary inequality \(p^{{\rm sep},0}_{c_\star0}+p^{{\rm sep},1}_{c_\star1}\leq1\) fails: the left side is greater than \(2(31/50)(93/100)=2883/2500>1\). Consequently, every armwise normalized \(p'\) satisfying \(\lVert p'-p^{\rm sep}\rVert_\infty<1/200\) is positive and \(T_0\)-compatible, while \(p'^0_{c_\star0}+p'^1_{c_\star1}>2883/2500-2/200>1\), so no such \(p'\) is representable under \(T_1\). Separately, \(p^{\rm gain}\) lies in the relative interior of the \(T_1\)-compatible set and \[ [L_{T_1}(p^{\rm gain}),U_{T_1}(p^{\rm gain})]=[-7/10,7/10]\subsetneq[-4/5,4/5]=[L_{T_0}(p^{\rm gain}),U_{T_0}(p^{\rm gain})]. \] There exists \(\eta_{\rm gain}>0\) such that every armwise normalized table \(p'\) with \(\lVert p'-p^{\rm gain}\rVert_\infty<\eta_{\rm gain}\) remains \(T_1\)-compatible and satisfies \([L_{T_1}(p'),U_{T_1}(p')]\subsetneq[L_{T_0}(p'),U_{T_0}(p')]\).
statements.justification: The two explicit witnesses show that selected trust is neither a relabeling of full exclusion nor observationally vacuous relative to trusting only the targets.
statements.gap: Song et al. characterize the full-exclusion model, but that result does not cover the displayed selected-trust response law; Gabriel et al. give isolated ternary comparisons without a nondegenerate strict-improvement region.
statements.consumer: A LEAP analyst can distinguish rejection of exclusion for an intermediate category from evidence that a separately trusted intermediate category sharpens the low-versus-high interval.

statements.statement: Under independent sampling, conditionally on \((N_0,N_1)\) with \(N_0N_1>0\), \(\Pr_P\bigl((L_T(p),U_T(p))\in\mathcal C_{\rm end}\mid N_0,N_1\bigr)\geq1-\alpha_{\rm conf}\). On the same event, the entire identified interval obeys \([L_T(p),U_T(p)]\subseteq\mathcal C_{\rm set}\). With the stipulated trivial output when an arm is empty, both conclusions hold unconditionally for every compatible \(P\), including affine-face ties, zero-probability cells, and zero-range faces.
statements.justification: One simultaneous concentration event controls both nonsmooth endpoints and the whole sharp set without selecting a derivative.
statements.gap: Song et al. provide simultaneous finite-sample Kullback--Leibler projection inference for the fully valid model; the proposed theorem gives a direct closed-form mixed-trust band, with no novelty claim for the concentration inequality itself.
statements.consumer: Sparse LEAP adherence tables receive honest whole-set uncertainty statements even when an active face ties or an exposure--outcome cell is empty.

statements.statement: Outlook question. Fix finite \((\mathcal E,T)\), \(\alpha_{\rm conf}\in(0,1)\), and \(\bar\rho>0\). Does the boundary-spliced active-face multiplier handle yield rectangles \(\mathcal C^G_n\) such that, over \(\mathfrak A_T(\bar\rho)\) with no lower bound on cell probabilities, active-face gaps, or affine-face variances, \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_k)\in\mathfrak A_T(\bar\rho)}\Pr_{P_n}\{(L_T(p_n),U_T(p_n))\in\mathcal C^G_n\}\geq1-\alpha_{\rm conf}.\] In addition, for every nonempty compact regular class \(\mathcal K(\varepsilon_{\rm reg},\gamma_{\rm reg},\sigma^2_{\rm reg})\), can the same rectangles satisfy \[\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal K}\frac{\mathbb E_P[w_{\rm tot}(\mathcal C^G_n)]}{\mathbb E_P[w_{\rm tot}(\mathcal C_{\rm end})]}<1,\] where total endpoint width is \(w_{\rm tot}([l_{\rm lo},l_{\rm hi}]\times[u_{\rm lo},u_{\rm hi}])=(l_{\rm hi}-l_{\rm lo})+(u_{\rm hi}-u_{\rm lo})\)?
statements.justification: This short Outlook isolates the genuinely open statistical rung with separate global validity and regular-class precision requirements.
statements.gap: Directional-differentiability and intersection-bound methods handle ties on regular classes, but their combination does not automatically cover simultaneously vanishing multinomial variances and boundary cells.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would replace the conservative production band by a shorter default while preserving a certified fallback for sparse adherence tables.

sampling_model.design: A binary randomized instrument \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), independent of the saturated response type.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(Z_i,X_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are independent and identically distributed draws from \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) takes values in finite \(\mathcal E\); categories in \(T\) share well-defined outcomes across instrument arms and categories in \(U\) impose no cross-arm outcome restriction.
sampling_model.overlap: Only instrument-arm positivity \(0<\rho<1\) is required; exposure cells may have probability zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All observable inputs are finite arm-cell probabilities estimated by empirical conditional frequencies; the finite-sample theorem does not estimate a smooth nuisance function.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For binary instrument, treatment, and outcome, the sharp average-treatment-effect interval is the maximum and minimum of eight affine response-type expressions.
With binary instrument and outcome and three well-defining exposure levels, the pairwise risk-difference bounds add the third-level terms to the classical binary list.

Under exclusion for every category, inequalities indexed by coordinate subsets characterize the compatible joint counterfactual distributions for arbitrary finite categorical instrument, treatment, and outcome.
For the stated finite response-function class, dual vertex enumeration yields valid and tight symbolic bounds for linear causal queries.
One multinomial Kullback--Leibler confidence region yields simultaneous finite-sample coverage for linear functionals of the fully valid categorical-IV counterfactual law.
Identification gains for binary average-treatment-effect bounds can be decomposed into contributions from instrument information and model features.

tldr: A binary randomized instrument and binary outcome are observed with an arbitrarily fine categorical exposure, but exclusion is credible only for a declared subset of categories. The sole identification kernel is a sharp pairwise-effect envelope governed by a two-diagonal capacity: each endpoint is the envelope of the eight Balke--Pearl affine pieces and exactly two pieces for every trusted nuisance category, with finite response laws attaining both endpoints. A perturbation-stable three-category family is selected-trust compatible on an open set yet violates a necessary full-exclusion inequality of Song et al.; a separate open region shows strict improvement over trusting only the two targets. A finite-sample whole-set band is valid at ties and zero cells, and a short Outlook asks for a uniformly valid boundary-spliced Gaussian rectangle with a strict expected-total-width gain on regular compact classes.

project_justification.gap: Published closed forms cover binary treatment and selected small-support coarsenings, while the arbitrary finite categorical-IV characterization imposes exclusion at every treatment level and leaves pairwise effects to generic optimization. The selected-trust regime strictly contains observed laws excluded by that full model, yet can strictly tighten the two-target Balke--Pearl envelope on an open set.
project_justification.niche: Applied adherence studies often have two interventionally meaningful target categories, several scientifically defensible intermediate categories, and residual categories for which no cross-arm exclusion statement is credible.
project_justification.fill: The two-diagonal transport reduction gives the sharp linear-size envelope and finite attaining response laws for this mixed-validity regime; trust updates, wholly untrusted refinements, and one-pass evaluation follow as consequences of the same formula.

related_work: Balke and Pearl derive the eight sharp affine ATE pieces for binary instrument, treatment, and outcome by response-function linear programming. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander distinguish well-defining from ill-defining coarsened exposure levels, obtain the ternary boundary formulas, and identify arbitrary exposure cardinality as ongoing work. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjolander, and Gabriel provide the symbolic primal--dual machinery that informs certification of every displayed face with a feasible response law. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson use finite-set Strassen theory to characterize arbitrary categorical IV models when exclusion holds at every treatment category. Their coupling construction informs the proof, but every law in the explicit perturbation-stable family \(p^{\rm sep}\) is selected-trust compatible throughout a positive-cell neighborhood and violates their necessary full-exclusion compatibility inequality; separately, the full-trust-compatible table \(p^{\rm gain}\) shows that trusting an intermediate category strictly tightens the two-target envelope on an open neighborhood. Bhadane, Mooij, Boeken, and Zoeter establish the observed full-exclusion compatibility boundary for binary instrument and outcome. VanderWeele and Hernan clarify why coarse treatment labels may conceal distinct versions, and Marshall shows that coarsening can distort conventional IV estimands; these papers provide context for the formula remark on wholly untrusted refinement. Zhang, Frazier, Poskitt, and Zhao analyze identification gains for binary ATE bounds; the categorywise active-face update is only a corollary of the sharp envelope. Du Toit and collaborators supply the LEAP experiment in which the sharp envelope determines whether separately justified intermediate consumption categories change the low-versus-high interval.
technical_internal_limitation: The phrase \(8+2|T\setminus\{a,b\}|\) denotes a complete affine evaluation list for each endpoint, not an assertion that every listed term is an irredundant facet on every lower-dimensional support stratum. Formula remark: a wholly untrusted refinement obeys \(L_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=L_T(p)\) and \(U_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=U_T(p)\); push a factual coupling forward through \(g\), and lift it by arbitrary disintegration within each untrusted fiber. Implementation note: compute the eight baseline faces, scan \(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\}\), update the lower maximum and upper minimum with the two category faces, and retain ties; this uses \(O(|\mathcal E|)\) arithmetic and \(O(1)\) auxiliary memory beyond the input and active-face output. These are formula and implementation consequences, not independent research targets. Producing a full attaining transport by generic augmenting paths is claimed only to terminate in finite polynomial time.
honest_scope: The sole identification kernel is the sharp-envelope theorem with its transport completion and finite endpoint-attaining laws. The perturbation-stable non-representability family and the separate open strict-gain region provide the load-bearing comparison with the full-exclusion model of Song et al.; the Hoeffding whole-set theorem supplies finite-sample coverage. The categorywise trust update is a one-line corollary, wholly untrusted refinement is a formula remark, and one-pass evaluation is an implementation note. The bounded computations are diagnostic evidence: the supplied checker reported agreement across \(840\) response-law linear programs, \(9{,}648\) exact rational endpoint constructions, and the exact LEAP interval \([-5073/31720,10/61]\); the denominator-three early-kill enumeration reported \(109{,}440\) exact endpoint constructions. These checks are not theorem premises. The Outlook question remains open over triangular arrays without cell, face-gap, or face-variance floors, while its strict precision comparison is restricted to nonempty compact regular classes. No monotonicity, exposure ordering, instrument relevance, exposure-cell positivity, or clinical justification of any trusted LEAP category is claimed.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: The Introduction, Results 1--4, the displayed ternary bounds in Section 2.3, the LEAP analysis, and the Discussion were read in the arXiv source. The Discussion explicitly asks whether the observed pattern extends to arbitrary exposure cardinality.
seed_details.question: For binary \(Z\) and \(Y\), arbitrary finite \(X\), and exclusion imposed only on a trusted subset containing \(a\) and \(b\), is the sharp interval for \(\theta_{ab}\) the eight Balke--Pearl pieces plus two affine pieces for each trusted nuisance category, with no mixed-nuisance pieces?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Song et al.'s coupling between one factual arm and a full vector of potential outcomes by a coupling of the two factual arm distributions whose forbidden relation is only a partial matching; then optimize two selected diagonal masses before completing the residual flow.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for mixed-validity categorical-IV bounds, partial-matching transport, arbitrary coarsened exposures, and citing work found Gabriel et al.'s ternary result and Song et al.'s full-validity characterization, but no arbitrary-cardinality selected-trust scalar envelope.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Song et al. because their Strassen inequalities already characterize every finite categorical IV model.
seed_details.rebuttal: Song et al. impose exclusion for every treatment category and leave the pairwise ATE as an optimization over a full counterfactual distribution. The perturbation-stable family \(q^{\rm sep}_{r,s,\tau,\lambda}\) is compatible under selected trust on an explicit positive-cell neighborhood but violates their observable full-exclusion inequality, while \(p^{\rm gain}\) gives a separate nondegenerate open region of strict improvement over the two-target envelope. Their theorem yields neither the \(8+2|T\setminus\{a,b\}|\) projection nor endpoint-attaining mixed-validity laws.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed uses the coupling-native M10 representation rather than presenting generic response-type linear programming as the contribution; the named focal object is the two-diagonal capacity \(D_T(p)\).

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: The LEAP table and Section 4 comparison were read. They show that the trusted third-level faces can tighten in principle but do not change the LEAP interval, without an observable if-and-only-if rule.
seed_details.question: Give necessary and sufficient observable strict inequalities for whether declaring one additional nuisance category trusted raises the lower endpoint, lowers the upper endpoint, or reduces interval width.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After deriving the affine endpoint envelope, compare the two new category faces to the old active envelope and distinguish strict replacement from a tie.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for categorical-IV identification gain, value of exclusion restrictions, and instrument identification power found Zhang et al.'s binary-ATE gain decomposition, but no category-specific trust criterion for coarsened treatments.
seed_details.red_team: Once the arbitrary-support affine list is proved, the strict update is an active-face comparison.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection is correct: the if-and-only-if inequalities are retained as a corollary and not as an independent novelty target.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The item is explicitly subordinated to the sharp-envelope theorem.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: The homocysteine analysis and Discussion were read. Three-bin and four-bin codings give the same numerical interval, but no structural refinement theorem is stated.
seed_details.question: Show that the sharp pairwise interval factors through armwise totals after every split or merge wholly inside the untrusted region, and exhibit why a refinement that changes the trusted intervention semantics need not be invariant.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Push a feasible factual-arm coupling forward through the aggregation map and lift it back by disintegrating only unrestricted rows and columns; the lift fails at the first trusted edge deletion crossed by the map.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing refinement invariance with coarsened-exposure IV bounds found Marshall's coarsening-bias result and VanderWeele--Hernan's treatment-version semantics, but no sharp-set quotient theorem under a selected trust boundary.
seed_details.red_team: A tautology because untrusted categories do not occur in the target potential outcomes.
seed_details.rebuttal: The pushforward and lift verify the claim, but after the envelope is established the equality is a structural corollary rather than a separate research kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The item is retained only as a consequence for exposure coding inside untrusted fibers.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Results 1 and 3 were read as the two endpoints of an all-or-nothing trust regime: exact exclusion adds faces, whereas direct instrument effects at the nuisance level collapse those gains.
seed_details.question: Replace hard trust by category-specific caps on direct instrument effects and derive a sharp piecewise-affine sensitivity path and the smallest violation radius at which a sign conclusion fails.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace deletion of a forbidden matching edge by a capacity on discrepant trusted-outcome flow and solve the resulting parametric transport dual across all breakpoints.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing categorical IV, exclusion sensitivity, direct-effect caps, and response-function bounds found Conley et al.'s linear plausibly-exogenous model and Duarte et al.'s generic numerical programs, but no closed-form category-specific path.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from generic parametric linear programming because every sensitivity radius enters a right-hand side.
seed_details.rebuttal: A numerical parametric program does not identify the complete breakpoint set, prove a closed-form envelope, or construct attaining laws uniformly in the radii; those are the substantive open steps.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed includes a critical violation radius and a sharp path, so it is not sufficient-only sensitivity.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Sections 1.2, 6, and 8 of version 6 were read. The paper obtains simultaneous finite-sample coverage from one multinomial Kullback--Leibler region and explicitly leaves less-conservative confidence intervals for future work.
seed_details.question: For fixed finite \((\mathcal E,T)\), \(\alpha_{\rm conf}\), and \(\bar\rho>0\), construct a boundary-spliced Gaussian-multiplier endpoint rectangle with uniform \(1-\alpha_{\rm conf}\) asymptotic coverage over \(T\)-compatible multinomial arrays having \(\rho_n\in[\bar\rho,1-\bar\rho]\) and no cell, face-gap, or variance floor, while obtaining a strict expected-total-width ratio below one relative to the Hoeffding rectangle on every nonempty compact class with fixed positive cell, unique-face-gap, and active-variance floors.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Estimate the directional derivative of the finite max/min map on a near-active face set, then prove anti-concentration and selection validity without dividing by a variance that may vanish.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for multiplier inference at affine-face ties and vanishing variance located Fang--Santos directional bootstrap and Chernozhukov--Lee--Rosen moment selection, but not their uniform combination at multinomial boundary cells.
seed_details.red_team: A finite envelope is a textbook directionally differentiable functional, so Fang and Santos already solve the problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their general derivative bootstrap does not by itself establish uniform validity for simultaneous sequences with zero multinomial cells and collapsing face variances, nor the proposed regular-interior precision comparison.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is a limit-law and uniformity frontier, labeled M11(c), rather than a bare inference modifier.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Theorem 1 and the sufficiency proof were read. Their armwise Strassen couplings are glued through a common full potential-outcome margin for arbitrary finite \(Z\).
seed_details.question: For finite multi-arm \(Z\) and binary \(Y\), characterize pairwise ATE bounds when exclusion holds only on a selected treatment subset, and determine whether a polynomial-size transport representation survives.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The two-arm direct coupling becomes a multi-marginal compatibility problem; the first unresolved move is whether the partial matching restrictions admit a common latent response law without exponentially many mixed-arm constraints.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for multi-arm instruments with category-specific treatment exclusion found Song et al.'s global exclusion model and Gabriel et al.'s three-arm small-support calculations, but no arbitrary mixed-trust theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by applying Song et al.'s theorem to each arm after deleting untrusted coordinates.
seed_details.rebuttal: Deleting coordinates removes the common consistency relation but does not remove their observed masses; pairwise arm couplings need not glue to one response law, so an additional multi-marginal step is required.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed identifies the failed gluing step rather than claiming a routine binary-to-multilevel extension.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Theorem 1, Theorem 2, and the nonredundancy count were read. For nonbinary \(Y\), non-singleton coordinate subsets generate additional necessary faces even under full trust.
seed_details.question: For ordered finite outcomes, find a computable sharp pairwise mean-effect support function under selected trust and determine whether the binary two-diagonal reduction becomes a bounded collection of outcome-level transports.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The edgewise minimum effect is no longer determined by membership in two binary diagonals; it becomes a min-cost transport problem with several outcome-cost levels and potentially mixed trusted-category cuts.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining nonbinary outcomes, categorical treatment, mixed exclusion, and sharp IV support functions found Song et al.'s full-trust polytope but no selected-trust closed form.
seed_details.red_team: Song et al.'s finite linear program already computes every linear mean contrast.
seed_details.rebuttal: That program assumes global exclusion and does not characterize the selected-trust feasible relation or an outcome-ordered transport support function; nevertheless the absence of a plausible linear-size closed form lowers feasibility.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The contribution would have to be the non-LP transport representation, not another generic linear program.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: Section 6 was read. Its single confidence region already covers any fixed finite collection of linear causal functionals simultaneously.
seed_details.question: Allow the analyst to select a trusted subset from the observed table and report valid post-selection bounds.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Project one simultaneous cell-probability region through every candidate trusted-set envelope before selection.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair is already occupied in substance by simultaneous multinomial-region projection.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Song et al.'s simultaneous confidence region because selection among finitely many projections cannot invalidate joint coverage.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; absent a new selection target or optimality statement, this is a corollary rather than a research kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Rejected as an inference add-on without an independent theorem shape.

seed_details.anchor_read_evidence: The Introduction, response-type linear-program construction, eight-piece ATE formulas, multivalued-treatment discussion, and final applications were read from the JASA article.
seed_details.question: Use mixed-trust pairwise intervals to learn a minimax-regret categorical treatment policy under unmeasured confounding.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Convert all pairwise sharp supports into a coherent conditional welfare uncertainty set and optimize policy regret over it.
seed_details.destination_search: A search for categorical partial-identification policy learning found Hruza et al. (2026), who already give categorical minimax loss, differentiable surrogates, and oracle rates using causal bounds as inputs.
seed_details.red_team: Subsumed by Hruza et al.'s categorical partial-identification learning framework once the bounds are supplied.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for this formulation; a distinct policy kernel would need cross-pair coherence or a sharper regret frontier not presently supported.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Rejected because the policy layer would merely consume the identification theorem.

literature_map.settled: Balke and Pearl derive the eight affine pieces for binary treatment. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander derive the small-support mixed-validity formulas and leave arbitrary exposure cardinality open. Sachs et al. show how finite response models yield tight symbolic bounds through primal and dual linear programs. Song et al. characterize arbitrary finite categorical IV models under exclusion at every treatment category by Strassen inequalities.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: No located paper gives the sharp scalar projection for arbitrary finite treatment support when exclusion is imposed only on a declared subset, or a proof that only two single-category pieces are added for each trusted nuisance category.
adjacent_threads: BalkePearl1997ImperfectCompliance, equations (4)--(5) and the multivalued-treatment discussion on pages 1173--1174.
GabrielSachsSjolander2025Coarsening, Sections 2.3--5 and the arbitrary-level question in the Discussion.
SachsJonzonSjolanderGabriel2023SymbolicBounds, Section 5 and Proposition 1 on dual vertex enumeration and tightness.
SongGuoChanRichardson2026CategoricalIV, Theorems 1--2 and Section 4 on finite-set Strassen sufficiency.
literature_map.closest_subsumption_check: Song et al. is the closest general paper, but its defining exclusion condition shares one potential outcome across instrument arms for every category; the proposed model deliberately replaces those shared outcomes by arm-specific factual labels on untrusted categories. Gabriel et al. is exact on the ternary boundary only. Neither subsumes the kernel.
literature_map.exemplars_used: The setup and motivation arc follow Gabriel et al.'s Introduction and LEAP application. The proof adapts Song et al.'s finite-set coupling relation at the first changed edge relation and Sachs et al.'s requirement that dual faces be certified by primal response laws.

literature_map.settled: Gabriel et al. show by formula and example that a trusted third category may add information but does not do so in LEAP. Song et al. establish weak set inclusion under the full categorical model. Zhang et al. decompose identification gains for binary ATE bounds, but not gains from validating one nuisance treatment category.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: The sharp-envelope theorem mechanically supplies exact strict affine inequalities when one nuisance category crosses the trust boundary; this is an applied consequence rather than a separate target.
adjacent_threads: GabrielSachsSjolander2025Coarsening, Section 4 and the LEAP example.
DuToitEtAl2015LEAP, randomized peanut-consumption trial and adherence variation.
literature_map.closest_subsumption_check: The 2025 identification-gain review concerns binary treatment and instrument-level identifying power; the categorywise check here is recorded only as a consequence of the new envelope.
literature_map.exemplars_used: Balke--Pearl's finite affine envelope supplies the active-face comparison, while Gabriel et al.'s LEAP discussion supplies the applied decision the criterion answers.

literature_map.settled: VanderWeele and Hernan distinguish coarse labels from treatment versions and show that merging versions generally changes intervention meaning. Marshall shows that treatment coarsening can bias conventional IV estimands. Gabriel et al. report equal bounds under two binning schemes without a general theorem.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: The endpoint formula implies equality under refinements confined to untrusted categories; the equality is retained as a coding corollary rather than an independent target.
adjacent_threads: VanderWeeleHernan2013Versions, Sections 1--2 and Proposition 8 on many-to-one coarsening and version-mixture interpretations.
literature_map.closest_subsumption_check: The version literature explains why unrestricted aggregation is not generally harmless, while the endpoint formula identifies the wholly untrusted case as a direct quotient consequence.
literature_map.exemplars_used: VanderWeele--Hernan supplies the intervention-level semantics; Song et al.'s coupling proof supplies the pushforward and lifting language.
